spec.title: User-local stewardship state and capability profiles

home.title: 1. State home

p.STATE-HOME: The state root is `~/.vibe/steward/`. It belongs to one operating-system user and may be shared by that user's successive central agents on the same machine. It is not committed, packaged, mirrored or treated as another contributor's authority.

home.fence: ~/.vibe/steward/ config.toml contexts/ <opaque-context-id>/ binding.toml settings.toml plan.toml GOAL.md GOAL-CLAUDE.txt custody.toml sessions/ handoffs/ records/

p.OPAQUE-CONTEXT-ID: `opaque-context-id` is a random UUID rendered as lowercase ASCII. It is an identity only; never parse meaning from it. Discovery scans `contexts/*/binding.toml`, so no mutable global context index is required.

p.CREATE-DEFAULTS: An owner-facing central session that finds no `config.toml` creates it before campaign work with the safe defaults below. Package installation itself never writes user state.

p.CONFIG-STRICT: The file is strict human-authored TOML. Unknown top-level keys are rejected and surfaced; they are not silently ignored. It is operator configuration, so JTD is intentionally out of scope.

binding.title: 3. Context binding

p.BINDING-TUPLE: A context binds an exact tuple: canonical repository root, canonical worktree root, Git common directory, and branch ref (or detached commit). Absolute paths are allowed because the file is local. A different branch or worktree may therefore use a different profile and plan without affecting teammates or sibling worktrees.

binding.fence: schema = 1 context_id = "3d7a79bf-5f27-4b88-9eaa-c8323df5cb03" project_name = "example" repository_root = "C:/work/example" worktree_root = "C:/work/example" git_common_dir = "C:/work/example/.git" revision_selector = "refs/heads/main"

p.CONTEXT-RESOLUTION: Resolution order is: an explicit context id named by the owner; an exact binding match; otherwise a new context. Zero matches creates; more than one exact match is corruption and must be surfaced, never settled by newest timestamp. Moving a checkout creates a new binding unless the owner explicitly repairs the old one.

settings.title: 4. Settings and live switching

p.SETTING-PRECEDENCE: Effective settings use this precedence: current owner instruction > current-context `settings.toml` > global `config.toml` > safe defaults. An owner instruction such as “switch the planning mode to ultra” updates the current context file immediately and applies within the same session; no `vibe` command or restart is required.

settings.fence: schema = 1 interaction_mode = "auto" planning_profile = "ultra" goal_node = "COMPILER-MODERNIZATION" updated_at = "2026-08-29T11:00:00Z" updated_by = "owner-chat"

p.SETTINGS-ORTHOGONAL: `interaction_mode` (`auto | collab`) controls how much the central coordinator narrates and asks. `planning_profile` (`ultra | standard`) controls planning scaffolding. `goal_node` selects the stable campaign/root node whose goal is projected; it is required whenever selection is not unique. The axes are independent. Historic input aliases `normal` and `medium` normalize to `standard`; stored values are canonical.

p.PROFILE-CANNOT-WAIVE: No profile may waive owner authority, destructive-action fences, lossless requirement coverage, central review, exact gates, fact promotion or handoff receipt.

p.SESSION-ID: Every central session chooses a fresh opaque `session_id` and writes a uniquely named record under `sessions/`. The record names harness, model as observed metadata, effective profile, start time and custody epoch. Model identity informs forensics; it never selects the profile automatically.

p.NO-SECRETS: Local records may carry absolute paths but never tokens, API keys, Authorization values, raw sensitive provider bodies or copied environment dumps. Record a secret source name or token-file path only when operationally necessary.
